sentences.show: He survived the first atomic bomb. Three days later, he was standing under the second.
Tsutomu Yamaguchi was a Mitsubishi engineer from Nagasaki.
In the summer of 1945, work sent him to Hiroshima.
On his last day, 6 August, he went back to the office for his forgotten stamp.
At 8:15, he looked up and saw a bomber, and two small parachutes.
Then a great flash. He was blown off his feet, 3 kilometres from the blast.
His eardrums burst. He was blinded for a while, and badly burned.
He spent the night in a shelter, in a city that was gone.
The next day, he took the train home. To Nagasaki.
On 9 August, wrapped in bandages, he went back to work.
He was telling his boss how one bomb had wiped out a whole city.
His boss called him crazy.
Then the room went white.
Fat Man had exploded over Nagasaki. Once again, about 3 kilometres away.
This time the blast didn't touch him. But for over a week, he burned with fever.
In 2009, he became the only person Japan officially recognised as surviving both.
At least 160 people were caught in both bombings.
He spent his last years asking the world to ban the bomb.
Tsutomu Yamaguchi died in 2010. He was 93.
He survived two atomic bombs to tell this story. Subscribe, and keep it alive.
